findings.title: Validated multi-edit programs can be only partially applied
findings.where: src/lib/structured-edit-dsl.ts:38 validates every anchor against the original source; src/lib/structured-edit-dsl.ts:105 applies edits sequentially and silently skips a missing later anchor; src/lib/structured-edit-arm-eval.ts:164 nevertheless returns schemaValid=true.
findings.what: A program such as source="abc" with edits [{find:"abc",replace:"x"},{find:"abc",replace:"y"}] passes validation because both anchors exist in the original source. Application produces only "x" because the second anchor was consumed, yet the constrained arm records the result as fully schema-valid with no errors. This makes validated edit output and repair telemetry non-reproducible from the validation claim and can silently accept a partial fix.
findings.fix: Validate edits by simulating them in order against evolving content, rejecting an edit when its anchor is absent at its application step; alternatively make applyEditDsl return a failure that runConstrainedEditRepair reports as schemaValid=false rather than skipping.
findings.acceptance: Add a regression test using source "abc" and two edits that both find "abc"; validation must fail with a domain-phrased error for the second edit, or constrained execution must return schemaValid=false and must not present the partial output as validated. Existing independent multi-edit behavior must remain passing.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the validator, applier, constrained-arm success branch, and current multi-edit tests at the immutable baseline. The validator checks source.includes(find) independently for every edit, the applier continues when an anchor disappears, and the caller unconditionally marks any initially validated program successful; no existing test covers interacting edits.
